title: Pytest declared console startup regression across six published pilots
scope: Retrospective execution of one ordinary declared public console entry and an unchanged existing test on all 18 sealed stock, revised Develop and prior Develop role patches from the six published pytest pilots.
finding: The exact declared pytest console entry crashes before collection on some proposals even though python -m pytest runs the same existing test successfully. Base and upstream merge both pass. This is public application breakage, beyond a private import-order or class-field introspection difference.
mechanism: The generated public console starts with _pytest.config:_console_main. On the failing dataclass variants it reaches ParameterSet while pytest is absent from sys.modules. The class already declares __module__="pytest"; Python dataclasses resolves its string annotations through sys.modules.get(cls.__module__).__dict__ and crashes. Running -m pytest first initializes the pytest package. Delaying only the public module assignment until pytest initialization repairs startup in the same revised source.

method.launcher_source:
#!/usr/local/bin/python3
# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
import re
import sys
if __name__ == '__main__':
    from _pytest.config import _console_main
    sys.argv[0] = re.sub(r'(-script\.pyw|\.exe)?$', '', sys.argv[0])
    sys.exit(_console_main())
method.launcher_generation: Pinned pip._vendor.distlib.scripts.ScriptMaker using unchanged pyproject.toml metadata. No historical dependency pytest wrapper, assessor shim, sitecustomize, module preloading or module monkeypatching.
method.configuration: Unchanged original pyproject.toml, natural argv and working directory, normal plugin loading; no -c, -o, plugin or autoload override. Fresh process and source copy for each route.
method.classification: A public CLI startup regression requires both console --help and the existing native test to exit 1 with the recorded dataclasses traceback, while the same native test through -m pytest exits 0 with 1 passed. A pass requires all three routes to exit 0 and both native routes to report 1 passed. Other or unavailable outcomes remain unknown.

reproduction.source:
"""Run inside the pinned Python image with the checkout and offline deps mounted."""
from pathlib import Path
import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import tomllib
from pip._vendor.distlib.scripts import ScriptMaker

parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
parser.add_argument('checkout', type=Path)
parser.add_argument('output', type=Path)
args = parser.parse_args()
work = args.checkout.resolve()
output = args.output.resolve()
output.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
metadata = tomllib.loads((work/'pyproject.toml').read_text())
entry = metadata['project']['scripts']['pytest']
assert entry == '_pytest.config:_console_main'
assert sys.version_info[:3] == (3, 13, 18)
assert 'pytest' not in sys.modules
maker = ScriptMaker(None, str(output/'bin'))
maker.variants = {''}
maker.clobber = True
maker.make('pytest = ' + entry)
launcher = output/'bin/pytest'
target = 'testing/test_mark_expression.py::test_empty_is_false'
commands = {
    'help-console': [str(launcher), '--help'],
    'native-console': [str(launcher), target],
    'native-module': [sys.executable, '-B', '-m', 'pytest', target],
}
env = dict(os.environ, PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE='1')
rows = {}
for name, command in commands.items():
    result = subprocess.run(command, cwd=work, env=env, capture_output=True)
    log = result.stdout + result.stderr
    (output/(name+'.log')).write_bytes(log)
    rows[name] = {'exit': result.returncode, 'log_sha256': hashlib.sha256(log).hexdigest()}
record = {'python': sys.version, 'entry': entry,
          'launcher_sha256': hashlib.sha256(launcher.read_bytes()).hexdigest(), 'routes': rows}
(output/'receipt.json').write_text(json.dumps(record, indent=2)+'\n')
print(json.dumps(record, sort_keys=True))

interpretation.supported: A consequential public CLI regression missed by the archived executable routes, and its observed incidence among these published role patches. Distinct fresh process entry routes can have different package-initialization state.
interpretation.limits: One retrospective known-repository sample. This does not establish an instruction treatment effect, transfer, an economic benefit, or a revised blind quality ranking. Two aliases with identical metadata are one entry implementation.
interpretation.legacy_metrics: All original scores, costs, readiness and missing/unknown measures remain as published. Prior and upstream soft PR quality remains unknown wherever it was not assessed.
